recommendations.title: Remove the single point of authorization: run ≥2 policies instances and cache decisions
recommendations.rationale: In experiment 6143d497b287 (risk LOW 2.0/10), API success fell to 75% during injection, TTR 42 s. Every Things/Search/Connectivity/Gateway request must enforce a policy, so the policies service is a hard dependency of the whole API. One instance means one crash equals a full outage until Pekko cluster sharding re-homes the policy actors on a replacement node.
steps: Run at least two instances: compose `deploy: {replicas: 2}` (or a `policies-2` service) or a Kubernetes Deployment with `replicas: 2` and a PodDisruptionBudget.

Keep the Pekko failure detector tuned for fast, stable detection — the compose file already sets it via `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` (`pekko.cluster.failure-detector.*`); verify `acceptable-heartbeat-pause` is ~3–5 s so sharding rebalances quickly without flapping.
Enable/raise the policy enforcer cache in the consuming services (Ditto `ditto.*.enforcement.cache` / `policy-enforcer-cache` settings) so recently used decisions survive a short policies outage.
Ensure the gateway `pekko.cluster.seed-nodes` list contains both policies instances or uses a discovery mechanism.
verify: Kill one policies container: API success rate during injection stays > 90% and no `cascade_beyond_hypothesis` finding is raised.

recommendations.title: Baseline observability: SLO alert rules and chaos annotations in Grafana
recommendations.rationale: In experiment 6143d497b287 (risk LOW 2.0/10), API success fell to 75% during injection, TTR 42 s. Whatever the specific fault, the first production improvement is knowing within a minute that users are affected. Alert on what the user sees (probe success, error rate, p95), not only on container liveness.
steps: Prometheus rules: `probe_success == 0 for 1m` (blackbox on `/api/2/things` through nginx), API error-rate SLO burn (`sum(rate(requests{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests[5m])) > 0.02`), and `histogram_quantile(0.95, ...) > 1s for 5m`.
Add a Grafana annotation (HTTP API `POST /api/annotations`, tag `chaos`) at the start and end of each Faultline experiment so latency spikes are attributable.
Dashboard the Docker health state per container (`container_health_status` via cAdvisor or a tiny exporter) next to the API SLIs.
verify: During the next experiment an alert fires within 60 s of the first API error and the Grafana graph shows the chaos window.
